system.summary: Four unrelated short ciphers: (a) figure substitution with a small code, (b) figures mixed with letters, (c) a ten-digit cipher, (d) homophonic figures with two codes.
system.sibling_key: Every 1653-60 royalist and Commonwealth key on cryptiana (Marshall, Barwick-Hyde, Stamford, Butler, Charles II intercepted, Kingston, Westrope, Hague agent/Blake) tried; none fits.
system.notes: Four separate systems, so types is undetermined for the set; NOTES read (a) as monoalphabetic letters plus a small code (8 code groups) and (d) as homophonic letters plus codes 226 243. nomenclator.entries counts the 10 code groups seen in (a) and (d).

prior_solution.where: Listed as undeciphered by Tomokiyo (cryptiana item #9); Birch's transcriptions are the only online witness and carry no decipherment.

tools: apply_keys.py (period keys scored by quadgram LM)
solve_a2.py (simulated annealing, bijective and homophonic modes)

solution.what: Extracted the four ciphertexts from Birch's Thurloe State Papers on British History Online.
Frequencies and repeats of each piece (analyze.py).
Applied every 1653-60 key from cryptiana to (a)-(d), scored by English/Dutch/French quadgrams; best -4.8 to -5.4 per quad against about -3.2 for real text.
Hill-climb on (a) with Dutch and French quadgram LMs, bijective and homophonic, 8 restarts: best -4.71 per quad, Dutch-looking fragments only.
(a) as a plain alphabetical key on 10-33 with any rotation or reversal.
(c) 'the king' for the 4-sign word forces an impossible name pattern; unresolvable at 16 symbols.
(d) cribs like 'horse' and 'hang' in the rich clear frame fit many assignments equally well.

Matched control for solve_a2.py on (a) (control.py, control_out.txt): synthetic texts in (a)'s exact layout (66+47+15 = 128 letters, 8 code groups), held-out Dutch/French/period-English text, 40 trials per cell, solver code unchanged. Recovered (>= 80% of letters): simple substitution 39/40 nl, 40/40 fr, 36/40 en; 25-symbol homophonic (homo, LAM 0.5, MAXH 2) 26/40 nl, 24/40 fr, 17/40 en. (a)'s own best (-4.71 nl, -4.57 fr per quad) lies below all 40 Dutch and all 40 French homophonic controls, so the negative is meaningful: (a) is long enough, and is not a <=2-homophone letter cipher of Dutch/French text as modelled.

outcome.method_basis: The four short intercepts printed in Birch's Thurloe State Papers resisted every 1653-60 key on cryptiana and quadgram annealing; a matched control shows piece (a) is long enough for the solver.
outcome.notes: Verdict STUCK: too short for cryptanalysis, no key online. Originals in Bodleian Rawlinson A, not digitised; sibling decipherments would be in the Nationaal Archief (a) and the Clarendon MSS (b-d), not online. Matched control run 2026-09-22 (control.py): the solver recovers synthetic texts of (a)'s layout (simple substitution 95-100%, 25-symbol homophonic 43-65% of trials), so the failure on (a) is meaningful, not a length artefact. The only commit (347fef4b5, 2026-09-15) has no model trailer.

gaps.detail: Matched control shows the length suffices for the solver, which still fails: system not the one modelled. Needs the key or a deciphered sibling despatch (Nationaal Archief), and Boreel's new code for the 8 code groups.
29 distinct homophonic symbols in 50 groups; key in the Clarendon MSS, not online.
